title: All-hands May 2026 - Talking points & Q&A (draft)
content:
Purpose:
- Draft talking points and Q&A for the May 2026 all-hands. This is an internal working doc (notes-to-self style) - still rough.

High-level framing (30s):
- Quick status: strong execution on inference performance and Dedicated capacity signups; healthy PLG momentum on Hosted API.
- Theme for the meeting: 'Serving at scale' - how we make inference predictable, affordable, and reliable for customers.
- Ask to leaders: come prepared with one short customer story and one operational improvement we shipped.

Business updates (1min):
- ARR / growth signals (high-level): continued growth in mid-market, several larger Dedicated deals in late Q1; funnel healthy. (Finance will share numbers in the deck.)
- GTM: new partner listing on two cloud marketplaces coming in Q2; should help APAC expansion.

Product highlights (2min):
- Hosted API: streaming and function-calling improvements rolled out; new SDK patch for edge-case crash fixed.
- Dedicated: launched burst capacity beta - early customers report 20% improvement in p99 under spikes.
- Private: completed first on-prem pilot with a regulated customer; integration docs updated.
- Optimize: auto-batching recommendations shipped to stage; initial customers saved ~12% on token cost.

Engineering & reliability (1min):
- Serving runtime: kernel selection improvements reduced median latency 8% on long context runs.
- SRE: new rollout policy safeguards reduced incident blast radius in two recent deploys.

People & org (45s):
- Hiring: still ramping infra and applied-ml; highlight two new ICs joining in April.
- Org tweaks: small realignment in product ops to streamline rollouts.
- Recognition: shoutouts (list to include ops on incident response, solutions eng on dedicated onboarding).

What I want people to walk away with (15s):
- We are shipping meaningful production improvements across the product surface that directly lower unit economics for customers.
- There is still a lot to do - especially on scale and ops - and leadership is aligned on priorities.

Manager asks (call to action):
- Bring a 1-line customer impact story to your team sync next week.
- Managers should post one improvement they rolled out in the last quarter to the #product-updates channel by end of week.

Draft Q&A (anticipated questions + suggested answers):
Q: How are we doing on latency SLAs for Hosted vs Dedicated?
A: Hosted has improved median latency across common configs; Dedicated offers stronger p99 controls via reserved capacity. We're tracking both in the console and will publish clearer benchmarks next month.

Q: Any update on pricing changes or rate limits?
A: No immediate pricing changes planned. We're testing new quota tooling to provide more predictable throttling behavior and clearer error messages. Any commercial changes would be communicated through customer channels first.

Q: How is the Private/on-prem roadmap progressing?
A: Pilot completed; next step is a bundled installer for air-gapped installs and KMS integrations. We'll surface a timeline in product notes next quarter.

Q: Are we seeing regressions in model quality after quantization/optimization?
A: We couple performance changes with eval suites and rollback policies. There have been a few small regressions in experimental quantization configs; those are gated behind canary and rollback.

Q: What metrics should managers watch to show we're improving unit economics?
A: Token cost per inference for representative workloads, p99 latency under typical load, and cache hit rates. Product will provide a one-pager with dashboards.

Notes to self / TODOs before slide deck final: 
- Sync with finance to confirm numbers and phrasing on ARR. (Evan)
- Ask product to provide a short case study from the Dedicated beta (Priya).
- Add 2-3 visuals: latency trend, cost-savings bar, roadmap timeline. (Liam to help with charts)
- Finalize name of theme and create title slide copy.
- Prepare a 1-paragraph script for exec to read, plus a 30s elevator version.

Tone / audience guidance:
- Keep things crisp and engineer-friendly; avoid marketing fluff. Focus on operational wins and customer impact.
- Be transparent about challenges (scale/perf) and specific next steps.

Version history (notes):
- 2026-03-02 initial draft
- 2026-03-04 updated to include Dedicated burst beta metrics and hiring notes.

Internal notes: this doc will be moved into the shared_drives/product/all-hands folder once finalized and will be converted into the slide deck.

-- end of draft --
